Reference Number: POC-AC94C7BBDE-82539
Date of Notice: 2026-08-01
Appeal Deadline: 2027-01-28
Requested Service/CPT: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA, Virginia
Type of Appeal: Pre-Service

To the Aetna Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29914 (hip arthroscopy with femoroplasty), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-01. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." This letter, together with the enclosed records from my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, is intended to supply the complete documentation necessary for Aetna to evaluate this request against its own clinical criteria.

I understand that Aetna applies Clinical Policy Bulletin Number: 0736, "Hip Preservation Surgery," to determine medical necessity for hip arthroscopy procedures including CPT 29914. That policy states:

"Aetna considers femoro-acetabular surgery, open or arthroscopic, for the treatment of hip impingement syndrome medically necessary for persons who fulfill all the following criteria: Diagnosis of definite femoro-acetabular impingement (FAI) defined by appropriate imaging studies (X-rays, MRI or CT scans), showing labral pathology (e.g. partial or full thickness labral tearing or labral damage) with one or more of the following: cam impingement (alpha angle greater than 50 degrees) pincer impingement (acetabular retroversion or coxa profunda) (center edge angle greater than or equal to 40 degrees), or pistol grip deformity (non-spherical femoral head shape); and"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip, performed 2026-06-15, documents an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees, which exceeds the 50-degree threshold in this criterion. This element of the policy is satisfied and is documented in the enclosed radiology report.

The policy further requires:

"Moderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI (hip or groin pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities, with duration of at least 6 months where diagnosis of FAI has been made as above; and"

I have had 18 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest, with sharp anterior groin pain on sitting and pivoting, and I am unable to run or squat. This exceeds the 6-month minimum duration and reflects the flexion-provoked pattern the policy describes.

The policy also requires:

"Positive impingement sign with sudden pain on 90 degree hip flexion with adduction and internal rotation or extension and external rotation; and"

Dr. Reyes' exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side with range of motion limited by pain, consistent with this criterion. Please see the enclosed exam note.

The policy further requires:

"Failure to respond to all available conservative treatment options including: activity modification (e.g., restriction of athletic pursuits and avoidance of symptomatic motion), pharmacological intervention (e.g., non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDS]), injections of local anesthetics into the joint) and physiotherapy. The treatment should be for at least 12 weeks in the past year with at least 6 weeks being formal physiotherapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist not virtual). Physical therapy (PT) needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history; and"

My record documents all of the required conservative-care modalities: NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief; a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-11 providing only 2 weeks of partial relief; and 10 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification (2026-04-20 through 2026-06-29, 18 visits completed), documented in the physical therapy discharge note enclosed with this appeal. The in-person PT course alone exceeds the 6-week minimum, and the overall course of NSAIDs, injection, and PT/activity modification spans well beyond 12 weeks in the past year, as reflected in the dates above. I am enclosing the PT discharge note and medication/injection records referenced in the denial notice as "incomplete"; if any additional claims-history confirmation of the PT visits is needed, I ask that Aetna identify precisely what is missing so it can be supplied promptly given the appeal deadline.

The policy also requires:

"Absence of advanced osteoarthritis change on pre-operative X-ray (Tonnis grade 2 or more) or severe cartilage injury (Outerbridge grade III or IV); and Absence of joint space narrowing on plain radiograph of the pelvis. Joint space is not less than 2 mm wide anywhere along the sourcil; and"

My MRI arthrogram of 2026-06-15 documents joint space preserved and Tonnis grade 0, well within these limits.

Finally, the policy requires:

"Member does not have generalized joint laxity especially in diseases connected with hypermobility of the joints, such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome; and Member does not have osteogenesis imperfecta; and All other potential sources of hip pain have been ruled out."

[Attestation from Dr. Reyes confirming absence of generalized joint laxity/hypermobility syndromes, absence of osteogenesis imperfecta, and that other potential sources of hip pain have been ruled out — to be enclosed]. My history includes no active infection and no untreated substance use, and my BMI is 29; I am a non-smoker.

In summary, the clinical record — MRI arthrogram findings, physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection records, and exam findings — addresses each element of CPB 0736's medical-necessity criteria for CPT 29914. I ask that Aetna reverse the denial and approve the requested hip arthroscopy with femoroplasty. If any specific document remains missing from Aetna's file, please identify it immediately in writing so it can be supplied well before the appeal deadline of 2027-01-28.

Please note: I have quoted only the language of CPB 0736 that I was able to obtain and verify directly; I have not been provided with, and this letter does not rely on, any additional plan document, and I request that Aetna send me a copy of the complete criteria and any other coverage document (including its effective/last-revised date) that was applied to this specific determination, in case any version or provision differs from what is quoted above.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the reference number under which it is being processed. I can be reached at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions.

Sincerely,

Reese Grant
Member ID: W386277495
[Signature]
[Date]
